_comment: Guided tour of the plugin manager. Every step points at a real control; two wait for the user to press it -- watching a button being pressed does not teach anyone where it is. 'name' is the emtk control (table, action or attr); 'key' / 'action' with the toolbar glyph label keep the legacy Qt tool's spotlight working.

steps.title: Everything ChiSurf found
steps.text: This table is one row per plugin. It is sorted and searchable: click a column header to sort, type in the filter box to narrow it down, and right-click the header to show columns that start hidden — Id, Source and Window state among them.

steps.title: Pick one
steps.text: Select any row. The right-hand window fills in with what that plugin is, which folder it lives in, and how it is wired to the rest.

await.hint: Click any row in the table.

steps.title: What it needs, and what needs it
steps.text:
The Requires column is what must load before this plugin — a module-level import. Required by is the reverse, and it is the one that matters before you switch anything off: those plugins stop working.

The Dependencies table on the right shows both directions at once, with the version bound and whether the plugin at the other end is actually installed.

steps.title: Switching a plugin off
steps.text: Disabled takes a plugin out of the menus without deleting anything. If other plugins require it, the status line tells you which ones — that is what the reverse dependency index is for.

steps.title: Putting one to hand
steps.text: Show in main toolbar pins the selected plugin to the main window's toolbar, so you do not have to walk the menus to reach the tool you use every day.

steps.title: Installing something new
steps.text: Install… takes a .zip (cancel the file chooser to pick a plugin folder instead). The manifest is validated first, so a broken plugin is refused with a reason instead of being copied in and silently ignored, and you are asked before anything is copied. It lands in your personal plugin directory (~/.chisurf/plugins), which needs no administrator rights.

steps.title: Nothing is saved until you say so
steps.text:
Changes here live in a working copy. Press Save to write them, or Revert to throw them away (it asks first). Menu changes appear the next time ChiSurf starts.

Try it now.

steps.title: Where to read more
steps.text: The Help button explains every control on this panel, and how plugin dependencies are declared in a manifest.
